name: int-format
axis: integer to decimal string, then reading the produced digits back
notes: n = integers formatted. VL uses `std:fmt`'s `toString`, JS `String(v)`, Rust `v.to_string()`, Python `str(v)`. One value in five is negative so the sign path is exercised. The LCG stays below 10^6 so the value sequence is exact in every runtime at any N. Python runs N=1_000_000, a 30x reduction. There is NO opt.vl. THE VL NUMBER MOVED ON 2026-09-01 AND THE RECORDED ONE IS NOT COMPARABLE: the ambient `toString(i32)` compiler builtin was retired (owner ruling) and `std:fmt`'s pure-VL renderer took its name, so what this benchmark used to time as the intrinsic is now the library. The variant that priced the two against each other - stdfmt.vl, measured 5.7x slower than the builtin - is deleted with the builtin, because main.vl IS that program now; that 5.7x is the standing cost of the move and the row needs a re-run before it is quoted again. (A hand-rolled digit loop through fromCodePoints measured 4.4x slower than the retired builtin, so it is not the way back.)
